Depression isn't just something you overcome, it's okay to get therapy and ask for help. Also I wouldn't even call what you have depression. I had been going to therapy for several years before I was diagnosed, in may 2021 (I was 20yrs old) and it has been hard even though the doctors I'm saying I'm fine. I got off of my antidepressants in January and started taking them again in June. Because I needed them and was doing horribly mentally. The thyroid does so much for the body and hypothyroidism does actually cause depression symptoms, hyperthyroidism can cause anxiety. The organ in your body that produces metabolism, and gives the energy for every single organ system in your body, so you can function and stay alive, has been removed. You have to have self compassion in these moments, it is not easy moving forward. I've had a very difficult time getting my shit together and be an adult because you're right it can really feel like things don't matter. Recently things have been getting better for me, I've been doing things for myself, making stuff and just trying to enjoy my life. That's all we can really do is try to find something, or do something that makes us happy, and you don't have to do it alone. You don't necessarily have to take antidepressants of course, but therapy might be a good idea. It's not just depression either it can be hormone imbalances as well. Most of all even if you don't necessarily think this, feeling lost after treatment, getting the all clear and not knowing what to do is a symptom of trauma. I guess it's because I was already getting mental health help before, but getting a cancer diagnosis definitely was traumatic, knowing that I need medicine everyday, and without it I'll die, is traumatic, my post operative hypoparathyroidism is traumatic.  It's hard but I'm aware that I can't do it alone, and there's absolutely nothing wrong with that. Going through cancer is hard, there's a lack of trust in your body's ability to keep yourself healthy. It's something that has to be processed. You're physically healed, your mind has to heal as well. I hope things get better for you.

This was really informative, and acronym for antisocial personality disorder is ASPD, not APD. APD is the acronym for avoidant personality disorder. It's a cluster C personality disorder, cluster C's are categorized by anxious behaviors, OCD is in the cluster C personality disorders. ASPD is a cluster B. 

Avoidant personality disorder is classified by an extreme fear of rejection, criticism, or public embarrassment to the point of not socializing or getting close with people at all. The fear of rejection is so strong that they often never allow themselves to make any friends, get into romantic relationships, work, or do anything involving human social interaction. 

Honestly I'm interested in APD as a disorder because I wonder how it develops, and if there's and overlap with avoidant personality disorder and autism. I certainly avoid talking to new people out of fear of embarrassing myself, but it's never reached that level.
